R	2022	02054TRSCB66MAI	TRESCA BROTHERS SAND & GRAVEL	66 MAIN ST	MILLIS	NORFOLK	MA	02054			TRESCA BROTHERS SAND & GRAVEL	66 MAIN ST	MILLIS	MA		02054	YES	NO	NO	NO	NO	NO	FRANCIS ROSSI	5083268827		FROSSI@TRESCACONCRETE.COM								327320	327331					42.1782	-71.3245	005784152		MAD005784152										MAR05CT82	MAR053048											NA				110003423180	1322220962017	7439-92-1	0007439921	Lead	NA	NO	PBT	NO	YES	NO	YES			717416	8.11	BSR	Barriers to Source Reduction	Cement and fly ash, which contain trace amounts of lead, are used in the manufacture of ready made concrete. The cement used by Tresca contains approximately 4.82 to 11.8 parts per million (ppm) of lead and the fly ash contains approximately 21.2 ppm of lead. Fly ash affects the plastic properties of concrete by improving workability, reducing water demand, reducing segregation and bleeding, and lower heat of hydration. Fly ash increases strength, reduces permeability, reduces corrosion of reinforcing steel, increases sulfate resistance, and reduces alkali-aggregate reaction. Concrete made with fly ash reaches its maximum strength more slowly than concrete made with Portland cement alone. The cement and fly ash are delivered in bulk and are added directly into the final product by an automated system. Waste concrete is recycled. The use of fly ash in concrete manufacturing is beneficial recycling. Fly ash is a byproduct of coal-fired electric generation plants. The use of fly ash byproduct in the manufacture of concrete offers several environmental advantages, such as diverting the material from the waste stream, reducing the energy investment in processing virgin materials, conserving virgin materials, and allaying pollution. R	2022	02054TRSCB66MAI	TRESCA BROTHERS SAND & GRAVEL	66 MAIN ST	MILLIS	NORFOLK	MA	02054			TRESCA BROTHERS SAND & GRAVEL	66 MAIN ST	MILLIS	MA		02054	YES	NO	NO	NO	NO	NO	FRANCIS ROSSI	5083268827		FROSSI@TRESCACONCRETE.COM								327320	327331					42.1782	-71.3245	005784152		MAD005784152										MAR05CT82	MAR053048											NA				110003423180	1322220961902	N511	N511	Nitrate compounds (water dissociable; reportable only when in aqueous solution)	NA	NO	TRI	NO	NO	NO	NO			717413	8.11	BSR	Barriers to Source Reduction	Nitrate compounds are contained in the admixtures MasterSet AC534, MasterLife CI 30, and Accelguard NCA. Tresca opted to use these admixtures because they conform to the most stringent chloride ion limits required by the concrete industry standards. Added chlorides can potentially initiate or promote the corrosion of reinforced steel. Chloride ion constraints are typically in place for concrete used in coastal environments. Other issues with using an admixture containing chlorides include drying shrinkage, creep, heat evolution, and resistance to sulfate attack. In addition, there is a potential energy savings by using MasterSet AC534, MasterLife CI 30, and Accelguard NCA in the manufacture of concrete block by reducing curing temperatures and/or steaming time. No nitrate compound waste is generated since the admixture is a raw material that is completely incorporated into the final product. The admixture is delivered and stored in bulk and is automatically dispensed, so no residue is generated. Tresca has considered many other alternative admixtures. However, none of the other admixtures were selected to be used. The other alternative admixtures considered have an increase in health or physical hazards, would use more nitrate compounds, have increased mixing times, decrease the strength of the concrete, have a shorter shelf life, and/or were not economically feasible. In addition, any alternative admixture selected must be approved by the Massachusetts Department of Transportation.	Barriers to P2

R	2022	0604WHYDRF34PRG	HYDROFERA LLC	340 PROGRESS DR	MANCHESTER	HARTFORD	CT	06042			HYDROFERA LLC	340 PROGRESS DR	MANCHESTER	CT		06042	YES	NO	NO	NO	NO	NO	SCOTT DUELL	8603377776		SCOTT.DUELL@ESSITY.COM								339113						41.79994	-72.50245	080660602												CTP002470										BSN MEDICAL LLC		BSN MEDICAL LLC				110059490787	1322220858094	50-00-0	0000050000	Formaldehyde	NA	NO	TRI	YES	YES	NO	NO			706512	8.11	GEM	General Environmental Management	Hydrofera maintains spill response supplies throughout the facility and trains personnel on response supplies location, type, and use. A response contractor, Clean Harbors, is also under contract with Hydrofera to be available 24/7 in the event of a non-incidental spill scenario at the facility. Since facility start-up, there have been no occurrences of non-incidental spills and Clean Harbors has not been utilized. Containment: Floors within production areas are lined with a protective epoxy coating to ensure potential spills cannot degrade or leach into the structure and the surrounding environment. The epoxy lining also extends up the lips of wall edges in wet manufacturing spaces to prevent releases through the building's structural seams. WastewaterTreatment tanks are manufactured of High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and are constructed with double walled containment capable of containing 110% of the capacity of each tank. Tanks are equipped with redundant high level alarms and automatic shut-off valves. Maintenance: The wastewater treatment system is monitored and maintained routinely. This includes monitoring of the effluent, and monthly/quarterly/annual preventativemaintenance on tanks, system controls, sensors, valves, pumps etc. Chemical Handling Procedures: In usechemical drums sit atop spill pallets inside the production areas. In the event of a spill in these areas, the materials will drain to floor sumps that are routed to the wastewater treatment system. Floor sumps are not connected in any fashion to any storm drainage system or exterior surfaces. Chemical Storage: New chemical drums are stored atop impermeable spill pallets in 1 of 4 chemical storage rooms, which are located immediately adjacent to an interior unloading area to minimize transport time and reduce risk of potential spills. The chemical storage rooms are completely enclosed, locked, ventilated, and separated from other chemicals that may result in hazardous reactivity if a mixed spill occurs. Only trained staff can access the chemical storage rooms and transport these chemicals to production areas.	Other Environmental Practices

(“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators. Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. Ford Motor Company has implemented a minimum quantity lubricant (MQL) machining process (also called near-dry machining) that reduces waste by more than80 percent for each engine we produce, also saving oil and water. This “dry-machining” process lubricates cutting tools with a fine spray of oil, rather than the conventional “wet-machining” that required large amounts of metalworking fluids and water to cool and lubricate the tools. For a typical production line, MQL can save more than 280,000 gallons of water per year. Additionally, MQL reduces the amount of oil needed to machine an engine or transmission by 80 percent or more. And by avoiding the need for a coolant system across most engine production lines, MQL helps to reduce energy use. MQL also improves plant air quality by eliminating the airborne mist produced by traditional wet-machining.	Miscellaneous

Ford Motor Company has implemented a minimum quantity lubricant (MQL) machining process (also called near-dry machining) that reduces waste by more than80 percent for each engine we produce, also saving oil and water. This “dry-machining” process lubricates cutting tools with a fine spray of oil, rather than the conventional “wet-machining” that required large amounts of metalworking fluids and water to cool and lubricate the tools. For a typical production line, MQL can save more than 280,000 gallons of water per year. Additionally, MQL reduces the amount of oil needed to machine an engine or transmission by 80 percent or more. And by avoiding the need for a coolant system across most engine production lines, MQL helps to reduce energy use. MQL also improves plant air quality by eliminating the airborne mist produced by traditional wet-machining.	Miscellaneous

(“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment. Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents. To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. (“RIS”) is a RCRA Part B Permitted Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility which engages in commercial hazardous waste incineration as its primary method of treatment to reduce both the quantity and hazards associated with industrial waste from off-site generators.  By nature, incineration reduces a chemical’s ignitability, toxicity, and reactivity, while reducing the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment.  Some wastes which RIS receives for treatment contain amounts of EPCRA Section 313 constituents.  EPCRA Section 313 constituent levels that RIS reports fluctuate due to waste composition and receipt frequency, which changes year over year.  RIS achieves greater than 99.99% destruction removal efficiency for any organic constituents which it treats, including EPCRA Section 313 chemicals.  To further eliminate the potential for toxic chemicals to enter the environment, RIS has programs in place such as a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan, Contingency Plan and a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.  RIS is ISO 14001/45001 certified and has a formal Waste Minimization Program to reduce wastes, while increasing recycling/reuse practices.  While RIS’ primary storage activities are associated with the incineration of waste and are reported accordingly, certain amounts of wastes which arrive on site are stored prior to shipment to another facility without repackaging.  Per EPA’s Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics EPCRA Section 313 Industry Guidance, RCRA Subtitle C TSD Facilities and Solvent Recovery Facilities, dated January 1999; “storage, relabeling, or redistribution of an EPCRA Section 313 chemical where no repackaging occurs does not constitute manufacturing, processing, or otherwise use of that chemical.”  As such, RIS has not included EPCRA Section 313 chemicals managed in this way in its reported quantities for otherwise use. The gas addressed by the FGTU is material that has been traditionally sent to flare as necessary without further sulfur-recovery treatment. In the event of malfunction or non-availability of this unit, such gases would still go directly to flare. The additional equipment and operation is aimed at reducing intermittent flare emissions of sulfur dioxide, particularly during certain periods of startup/shutdown and malfunction. Sulfur material captured during such periods is stored on-site as amine salts for subsequent treatment and resource recovery in the existing fuel gas treatment facility (MSCC's amine unit) and MSCC's sulfur recovery plant during normal operation of those portions of the facility. The FGTU uses an amine treatment contactor to remove H2S from selected gases during these situations prior to flaring, along with liquid storage. Therefore, we have reported on this de minimis-level impurity because it is believed to be incidentally formed (and then destroyed) in the processes in amounts aggregately exceeding the threshold 25,000 lbs. per year. Ford Motor Company has implemented a minimum quantity lubricant (MQL) machining process (also called near-dry machining) that reduces waste by more than 80 percent for each engine we produce, also saving oil and water. This “dry-machining” process lubricates cutting tools with a fine spray of oil, rather than the conventional “wet-machining” that required large amounts of metalworking fluids and water to cool and lubricate the tools. For a typical production line, MQL can save more than 280,000 gallons of water per year.  Additionally, MQL reduces the amount of oil needed to machine an engine or transmission by 80 percent or more. And by avoiding the need for a coolant system across most engine production lines, MQL helps to reduce energy use. MQL also improves plant air quality by eliminating the airborne mist produced by traditional wet-machining.	Miscellaneous

Ford Motor Company has implemented a minimum quantity lubricant (MQL) machining process (also called near-dry machining) that reduces waste by more than 80 percent for each engine we produce, also saving oil and water. Additionally, MQL reduces the amount of oil needed to machine an engine or transmission by 80 percent or more. And by avoiding the need for a coolant system across most engine production lines, MQL helps to reduce energy use. MQL also improves plant air quality by eliminating the airborne mist produced by traditional wet-machining.	Miscellaneous
